title: PIAS1-mediated GSK3β SUMOylation exacerbates tauopathy and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s disease models

comments: The clinical association of PIAS1 polymorphisms with AD risk provides strong human genetic support, making the PIAS1-GSK3β axis a highly compelling therapeutic target.

title: METTL5-mediated rRNA modification controls prostate cancer progression through the IRF7/DNA2 axis and mitophagy regulation
task: Elucidate METTL5-rRNA m6A modification's role in prostate cancer progression through selective translational control
key_results: METTL5 catalyzes m6A modification at A1832 of 18S rRNA; preferentially enhances translation of mRNAs with GCACGN(2-4)CC motif in 5' UTR; selectively upregulates IRF7, which induces DNA2; DNA2 preserves mitochondrial function; METTL5 inhibition via locked nucleic acids suppresses tumor growth in vivo without systemic toxicity
comments: The elegant integration of rRNA modification, selective translational control, and metabolic rewiring through a motif-specific mechanism is mechanistically sophisticated and therapeutically actionable.

model_io.model: prostate cancer cell lines, transgenic mouse models, and primary tumor tissues

hypotheses.hypothesis: METTL5-dependent rRNA modification promotes prostate cancer through selective IRF7/DNA2-mediated mitochondrial homeostasis

title: Antisense oligonucleotides treatment uncovers differences in the modulation of dysregulated intracellular pathways in Spinal Muscular Atrophy motoneurons

title: Macrophage CCRL2 promotes NLRP3 inflammasome activation to exacerbate atherosclerosis
task: Characterize CCRL2's role in promoting NLRP3 inflammasome activation in atherosclerotic macrophages
key_results: CCRL2 expression increases in atherosclerotic lesions with predominance in inflammatory macrophages; hematopoietic CCRL2 deletion in Apoe-/- mice attenuated atherosclerosis by reducing plaque burden, macrophage accumulation, and inflammasome activation without affecting blood lipids; CCRL2 is endocytosed to early endosomes where it interacts with NLRP3; macrophage-targeted Ccrl2-siRNA nanoparticles suppressed atherosclerosis progression and IL-1β production
comments: CCRL2 represents a rare example of a compartmentalized inflammasome regulator, with endosomal localization being critical for its function—a mechanistic insight that could guide future drug targeting.

model_io.model: human atherosclerotic lesions, Apoe-/- mice, macrophage cell lines, and nanoparticle-mediated siRNA delivery

hypotheses.hypothesis: Macrophage CCRL2 promotes atherosclerosis by facilitating NLRP3 inflammasome activation via endosomal localization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CCRL2 deletion and siRNA targeting both attenuate atherosclerosis by reducing inflammasome-dependent IL-1β production

title: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of hepatic TMEM141 attenuates MASH and fibrosis via the ROS-HNF4α signaling pathway
task: Establish TMEM141's role in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through ROS-HNF4α signaling

comments: The counterintuitive finding that TMEM141 downregulation (normally seen in disease) is actually protective when enforced genetically suggests complex compensatory mechanisms in natural disease progression.

model_io.model: MASLD/MASH patient tissues, mouse models (HFCF diet), hepatocyte cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: TMEM141 promotes MASH progression by enhancing mitochondrial ROS production and suppressing HNF4α

title: Folding a broken genome: the versatile roles of cohesin in genome maintenance
task: Review cohesin's dual roles in 3D genome organization and DNA repair during double-strand break response
key_results: Cohesin tethers sister chromatids and extrudes chromatin loops; cohesin-mediated loop structures facilitate DNA double-strand break signaling and promote long-range chromatin motions required for homologous recombination repair
comments: This review synthesizes emerging evidence that cohesin's loop extrusion function extends beyond gene regulation to directly support DSB repair, positioning cohesin as a central genome maintenance hub.

title: CST complex promotes second-strand synthesis in break-induced replication
task: Elucidate CST complex's role in second-strand synthesis during break-induced DNA replication (BIR)
key_results: CST-deficient cells show normal 5' resection and D-loop formation but impaired second-strand synthesis; yeast and human CST promote second-strand synthesis by enhancing DNA polymerase α-primase activity in biochemical reconstitution experiments
comments: This work resolves a long-standing gap in BIR mechanism and suggests CST has dual roles beyond telomere regulation, though the molecular details of CST-pol α interaction require further investigation.

model_io.model: yeast cells lacking Cdc13-Stn1-Ten1 (CST), human cells, and biochemical reconstitution with DNA substrates

hypotheses.hypothesis: CST complex is required for efficient second-strand synthesis in BIR
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CST-deficient cells have impaired second-strand synthesis; CST promotes pol α-primase activity in vitro

title: Identification of a sequence element regulating H3K9 methylation at the ap2-g locus in Plasmodium falciparum

model_io.model: P. falciparum parasites (erythrocytic stage)

hypotheses.hypothesis: URE-G is a cis-element required for H3K9me3-mediated ap2-g silencing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; URE-G deletion reduces H3K9 methylation and derepresses AP2-G expression
